overview:
Techspert is the world's first AI-driven expert network, founded in 2016 by Graham Mills and David Holden-White in Cambridge, UK. The company's core innovation is its deep search technology — machine learning algorithms that autonomously crawl online content in real time to identify the most qualified expert for any topic, no matter how niche. The platform can review profiles of 280 million potential experts from academic journals, medical registries, patent databases, and biographical data in minutes.

Techspert has carved out a strong position in healthcare and life sciences, where finding experts in highly specialized therapeutic areas, rare diseases, and cutting-edge research requires searching beyond traditional expert databases. The company positions itself as a global leader in healthcare and life sciences expert connections, complementing its AI-driven sourcing with a growing international team in Cambridge and Houston.

The company has raised approximately £13.5 million across three funding rounds, backed by investors including BGF, Nauta Capital, Cambridge Angels, and Angel CoFund. Techspert has delivered projects in 100+ geographies, demonstrating the global reach of its AI-powered expert discovery engine.

history.narrative:
Graham Mills, David Holden-White, and Hari Jackson (CTO) founded Techspert (originally as 'Biotechspert') in 2016 in Cambridge, UK. David holds a Master's in Biochemistry from Oxford and a Master's in Bioscience Enterprise from Cambridge; he previously worked as a biotech patent attorney and in corporate development. Hari Jackson, an AI expert with advanced degrees from Cambridge and Oxford, built the core AI search technology.

The company raised £1 million in December 2018 from Cambridge Angels and other investors. In February 2020, Techspert closed a £3.75 million Series A led by Nauta Capital. The biggest equity round came in October 2021: $12M from BGF and Nauta Capital, funding the Houston, Texas office opening. In 2023, Techspert secured venture debt from Western Technology Investment, launched the ECHO Ask generative AI assistant (first-to-market among expert networks), and acquired data/assets from FirstThought after that healthcare expert network went bankrupt. In February 2026, Techspert received £5M growth credit from Palatine Growth Credit. Total funding: approximately $21.8M.

aiPlatform.narrative:
Techspert's AI search engine, developed by Cambridge data scientists over 5+ years, scans billions of online data points in real time — publications, clinical trials, regulatory docs, news — indexing 280M+ expert profiles globally. A knowledge graph covering millions of expertise areas enriches queries, and probabilistic models refine matching. Experts are scored across four dimensions: experience, communication skills, influence, and commercial insight. The platform achieves a 70% expert acceptance rate (double the industry average) and 1 in 3-4 experts are first-time consultants.

In 2023, Techspert launched ECHO Ask — the first generative AI assistant in the expert network industry. ECHO Ask enables cross-interview querying, quote compilation, segment summaries, and CSV exports, sourcing answers exclusively from call content to prevent hallucination. ECHO is HIPAA-compliant with no data retained by third parties and customer data never used to train models.

complianceExtended.narrative: Techspert maintains standard compliance protocols appropriate for its focus on technical and scientific consultations. The company's AI-assisted credential verification cross-references expert qualifications against public databases, adding a layer of automated validation on top of manual review. As a UK-based company, Techspert operates under GDPR requirements for data handling of the professional profiles it processes.

clientFit.narrative: Techspert is purpose-built for clients who need to find niche technical and scientific experts that traditional expert networks cannot source. The platform excels when the required expertise is highly specialized — rare diseases, emerging technologies, regulatory science — and the experts are not registered on any database. Clients seeking general business expertise or high-volume, routine expert calls may find traditional networks more efficient.
